note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Three days of diarrhoea with abdominal pain and vomiting (vomited this morning). Possible food exposure (strawberries at breakfast) and anxiety noted as potential contributing factors.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset about three days ago; diarrhoea ongoing, not clearly improving or worsening; central abdominal pain; vomiting this morning; currently able to eat lightly but frequent toilet visits.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None reported (no throat swelling, voice change, dysphagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, dyspnea, facial/lip/uvular swelling).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Asthma; uses inhaler (brand not specified); NKDA.
  - Family history: father died of bowel cancer (10 years ago) with concern about personal risk.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: NKDA (allergy status documented as NKDA; dose/route/frequency not documented for inhaler).
  - Current medications: Asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  - Not explicitly described; no acute social support details provided.
- Additional notes from clinician:
  - Concern about potential GI cause; patient not febrile at presentation; able to walk and talk.

Objective:
- Observable findings:
  - Abdominal tenderness to palpation (pain elicited with pressing on the abdomen; central/around the belly button).
- Airway/breathing:
  - Patient able to speak in full sentences; no reported stridor or acute respiratory distress; asthma history noted but no acute wheeze described.
- Mental status/others:
  - Not reported as dizzy or syncope.
- Vitals/exam findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of other person:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Primary impression:
  - Gastroenteritis with diarrhoea and vomiting, likely infectious; abdominal pain present; no alarming ENT findings or airway compromise.
- Justifications:
  - Onset within three days with persistent diarrhoea and vomiting; central abdominal pain; no blood in stool or vomit reported; no fever noted; able to maintain conversation and function.
- Conflicts:
  - No conflicts noted in the transcript.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advised:
  - Drink lots of water and fluids; monitor for fever.
  - Stay home for the time being until slightly better.
  - Antibiotics not recommended; antibiotics do not help in this scenario.
  - If symptoms worsen (e.g., high fever, inability to keep fluids down, dehydration, blood in stool/vomit, severe abdominal pain), go to GP.
- Specific instructions to patient/caregiver:
  - “If you feel you’re getting much worse, then I would suggest you go and see your GP in real life, in real life, in real life, in person, so they can loot at your belly.”
  - Remain at home and await improvement; book an in-person GP appointment if not better in a couple of days.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Fever development; dehydration signs; inability to keep fluids down; vomiting persists; blood in stool or vomit; worsening abdominal pain.
- Follow-up:
  - Reassess with GP in real life if symptoms persist or worsen; no ENT/allergy-specific referral indicated at this time.
- COVID-19 vaccine relevance:
  - Not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions:
  - As stated: “go and see your GP in real life, in real life, in real life, in person, so they can loot at your belly.”

Document_quality:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not recorded.
  - No documented hydration status (e.g., oral intake balance, signs of dehydration) or weight.
  - No explicit ENT examination findings (not applicable here) or GI examination details beyond mild abdominal tenderness.
  - No stool characteristics beyond diarrhoea; no fever measurement; no imaging or labs ordered.
- Internal conflicts:
  - None noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation clear; some filler phrases and minor repetitions due to telemedicine style; clinical content consistent with gastroenteritis management.
